title.narrative: Financial Sector Stability and Reforms Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The program adopts a programmatic policy-based loan (PBL) modality with two subprograms of $200 million each to properly sequence reforms and ensure the needed flexibility while implementing multi-year policy reforms in a crisis period. Subprogram 1 prioritizes immediate reforms to enhance the crisis management regulatory framework and stabilizing the financial sector while subprogram 2 prioritizes follow-on reforms to build a resilient and inclusive financial system. It will be supported by an attached transaction technical assistance (TA) for subprogram 2 and post-program partnership framework (PPPF) activities. A programmatic approach that combines policy-based loans, TA, and knowledge support was selected as it allows complex and challenging reforms to be addressed comprehensively.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.
08 Dec 2023 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-approves-200-million-sustain-economic-stabilization-efforts-sri-lanka

1.1. Cabinet approved the establishment of the Crisis Management Committee (CMC) and the Monetary Board of CBSL operationalized the CMC with a mandate to coordinate urgent actions required to mitigate liquidity and solvency crisis comprising representatives from MOF and CBSL.
1.2. In accordance with CBSL directions, all licensed banks with assets more than Rs1 trillion submitted recovery plans to CBSL in 2022 and 2023.

1.3. The Monetary Board of CBSL approved and implemented a revised framework for Emergency Loans and Advances, including an expanded list of eligible collateral for all banks, to discharge its function more effectively as Lender of Last Resort.

1.4. Parliament approved the Banking (Special Provisions) Bill strengthening the Central Bank of Sri Lanka's mandate as a resolution authority and granting broader statutory provisions for resolution and orderly winding down of banks.
2.1. CBSL completed an Asset Quality Review (AQR) of 9 largest domestic banks to identify stresses and risks building up on their balance sheets for potential recapitalization.

2.2. CBSL issued proposed directions for industry consultation to mitigate credit concentration risks on bank balance sheets which include exposure limits to large borrowers, including state owned enterprises and group holding companies.

2.3. The Cabinet approved and submitted to Parliament for approval of the Secured Transaction Bill to enhance collateralized lending and asset quality by improving transparency and acceptance of movable assets as collateral pledged by SME borrowers.

2.4. MOF incorporated a National Credit Guarantee Institution, with at least 2 out of 9 women directors to (i) improve asset quality on loans with partial collateral, (ii) reduce potential credit risks to banks and non-banks in lending to micro, small, and medium-sized enterprise (including women led businesses).

3.1. CBSL issued Directions to Licensed Banks and Licensed Finance Companies mandating recording of depositor details under a unique identification number to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the compensation payment process.

3.2. CBSL issued operating instructions and started collecting data from all licensed banks and licensed finance companies on MSME borrowers including gender disaggregated (sex disaggregated data) reports for better and targeted credit access to women led SMEs.

3.3. The Cabinet approved and submitted to Parliament the Micro Finance and Credit Regulatory Bill to establish a separate credit regulatory authority to better regulate lending by microfinance institutions.

3.4. CBSL issued a direction on Sustainable Finance Activities of Licensed Banks in line with the Road Map for Sustainable Finance and Sri Lanka Green Finance Taxonomy published by CBSL promoting sustainable economy and finance practices.
